payload.rationale: The forecast relies on the strong early September EIA gasoline price data, historical seasonal adjustment factors for September, and recent core CPI trends. Gasoline prices have surged in the first half of September, and September historically has a positive seasonal adjustment factor for gasoline (SA change is typically ~2% higher than NSA change). This combination strongly suggests a significant positive contribution from energy to the headline CPI, making a print of 0.3% or higher very likely.
limitations: Only two weeks of September EIA gasoline data are available, leaving the second half of the month uncertain.
Core CPI and food components could unexpectedly soften, offsetting energy gains.
EIA weekly prices are an approximation of the BLS sampling methodology.
payload.partition_justification: The scenarios are partitioned based on the trajectory of gasoline prices in the remainder of September and the behavior of core inflation, which are the primary drivers of headline CPI variance.

scenarios.description: Gasoline prices remain elevated or rise further in late September, and core CPI remains sticky at 0.2% to 0.3%.
scenarios.rationale: With EIA prices already at $4.455 by mid-September, a sustained high price level combined with a ~2% positive seasonal adjustment will add ~0.2% to 0.3% to headline CPI alone, guaranteeing a print >0.2%.

scenarios.description: Gasoline prices retrace some of their early September gains, and core CPI softens to 0.1% to 0.2%.
scenarios.rationale: Even if gasoline prices drop back to August levels, the high early-month prints and positive seasonal adjustment will likely keep energy's contribution positive. A softer core makes a 0.2% print possible, but 0.3% remains more likely.
unknowns: Pace of gasoline price mean reversion
Shelter and used car price dynamics

scenarios.description: Gasoline prices collapse in the second half of September, and core CPI comes in unusually weak (0.0% to 0.1%).
scenarios.rationale: A sharp drop in energy prices could fully offset the early month surge, leading to a negative energy contribution. Combined with a weak core, headline CPI would likely round to 0.1% or 0.2%.
unknowns: Potential for sudden negative supply/demand shocks in oil markets
